category_title: Students who disengage and exhibit behavioral issues when curriculum lacks challenge and teacher communication is perceived as indirect
minimal_context: The tutor is explaining a new mathematical concept to Raheem on the board.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's look at this math concept on the board. We need to utilize the inverse operations to isolate the variable by systematically applying the properties of equality.

STUDENT: The way you teach is so boring. It's not interesting. You're playing with words. You don't put any style or pizzazz into it.

TUTOR: Please just follow along. We must transpose the constant term to the adjacent side of the equation.

STUDENT: You put the work in difficult terms when it could be explained plain and simple.

TUTOR: I mean we just subtract the number from both sides.

STUDENT: Why you just didn't say that in the first place instead of going through all this? You really beat around the bush instead of just getting down to the point.

options.A: Explain the math concepts in plain and simple terms, just getting down to the point.
options.B: Provide opportunities for the student to respond at a rate of four to six responses per minute.
options.C: Redirect the student's nonproductive behavior during the math explanation on the board.
options.D: Use culturally relevant math problem contexts that align with the student's leisure activities.
